author: EDantes
text_post: Not really, hunter-gatherer societies today live to be about 70 years old; most of the low life expectancy was the result of disease or warfare (such as the AIDs crisis in Africa). In the earliest tribes the natural order and gender roles seem to have been preserved very well; it's when men started tampering too much with nature and creating massive civilizations that everything went downhill. Today the progressive narrative is that people started off as "savages" and have been slowly "progressing" along with technology; but in reality I see it the opposite; all of our efforts are simply undoing the damage we did when we created civilization. Unfortunately today we tend to over-value "safety and convenience" and view those without it as destitute, which plays a role in our turning to the welfare state to save us from ourselves versus being individually productive.  Not to mention technology and progress aren't always synonymous (the Nazis had much more scientific and technological knowledge than the ancient Greek philosophers, for example).
